title: Dangerous dance jobs at Delacroix Island
summary: He describes brawling crowds at Delacroix Island, a trick played to get him on the job with Kid Howard and Sidney Brown, and why he never went back.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And we had plenty of messages, man. We went out in the country and played music. I went with Kid Howard one time. And I had said I never was going out there no more. Out in Grand Isle. Oh yeah. And then that other place down around Michelle Beach.
Out at West End? No, no.

Down that way? Not that out in Semonaut Parish. Oh no, I don't know. There's never been down there much. There's Delacro Island. Delacro Island, that's it. Is that it? Yeah. I seen them people fight down there so that it was scary to look at them. It was cold. It was cold and raining. Ice fall on the ground. They fight and they cut up one another and roll all underneath the cars and everything. You heard that time when they whip up Papa Celestad's band? No, nobody ever told us that. Yeah, the whip up Papa Celestad's band. Down at Delacro Island? Down at Delacro Island. Down at the top of each car. They paid for that, they told me. After that they got the... Are they all drunk or something? Oh they did. They'd never be sober. Yeah. Not down there. And so I said I was never going out there no more. So some fellas, they had me to go down there. They told me I was going to Shell Beach. After I noticed the road you were taking, I said, Hey man, you're not going to Shell Beach. Oh, I didn't want to tell you because I know you wasn't going to go down there. And we needed a drummer tonight. And everything was going to come out all right. When the girls down there, they hit Kid Howard. They just kept the truck and bottles and things. And finally, they hit the bass player. Sidney Brown. Oh yeah. He hit Sidney Brown too. So I said, Y'all fellas are going to go and tell the man that what's happening. I said, Because I don't want to get in no trouble out here. So finally they reported to the man. He said, There ain't nothing going to happen to y'all. I said, Well listen mister. I said, Ain't nothing going to happen. You're going to be here and we hit that road and they make a roadblock and we can't go no further. Something will happen. So he said, You boy at home. He said, Ain't nothing going to happen. Well sure enough, Nothing didn't happen. But I said, If it didn't happen that time, It's not going to happen because I ain't going down there to move. And I never did go down there either. That was my last trip down there. No way.
Was there a picnic ground there or something?
